schema,\n// and loads the users and combat caches from durable storage. It must be called\n// once before the HTTP server starts accepting requests.\nfunc initDB() error {\n\tvar err error\n\tdb, err = sql.Open(\"sqlite\", dbFile)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"open sqlite: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif err := db.Ping(); All HTTP endpoints, response bodies, status codes, validation rules, and persistence semantics are preserved from the prior cumulative `dm-tools` suite. The only changes are structural: files are split by domain, duplication is reduced, and invariants are documented.\n\n## Quick start\n\n```bash\n# run the server in the foreground on the port given by the PORT env var\nPORT=8080 ./run.sh\n```\n\nIf `PORT` is not set, the server listens on `127.0.0.1:8080` by default.\n\nVerify the server is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:8080/health\n```\n\nThe SQLite database is stored in `./game.db`. The first startup creates the schema automatically.\n\n## Entry point and routing\n\n- `main.go` is the only entry point. It initializes the database, creates an `http.ServeMux`, registers all handlers, and calls `http.ListenAndServe` on `127.0.0.1:$PORT`.\n- Routes are grouped by domain: core rules, auth, combat, storage, compendium, campaigns, PHB rules, and DM tools. Each handler is implemented in a `handlers_*.go` file.\n\n## Major files and modules\n\n| File | Responsibility |\n|------|----------------|\n| `main.go` | Server entry point and route table. |\n| `models.go` | All domain structs (`user`, `session`, `monster`, `item`, `campaign`, `character`, `campaignEvent`, etc.). |\n| `rules.go` | Static lookup tables (CR XP, encounter thresholds, loot table, spell slots) and pure calculation helpers (`abilityModifier`, `proficiencyBonus`, `computeInitiative`, `computeEncounterMetrics`, `recommendationFor`, `lootForTier`, `recapOpenThreads`). |\n| `db.go` | SQLite connection setup, schema DDL, and all DB helper functions. |\n| `state.go` | Package-level mutable state (`db`, `users`, `combat`, `initMu`/`initialized`). |\n| `handlers_core.go` | Shared JSON response helpers and core rule endpoints (`/health`, dice, ability checks, adjusted XP, initiative, ability modifier, proficiency, derived stats). |\n| `handlers_auth.go` | Password hashing and the `/v1/auth/*` endpoints. |\n| `handlers_combat.go` | In-memory combat sessions (`/v1/combat/sessions/*`). |\n| `handlers_storage.go` | Storage status and reset (`/v1/storage/*`). |\n| `handlers_compendium.go` | Monster and item CRUD (`/v1/compendium/*`). |\n| `handlers_campaign.go` | Campaigns, characters, events, and campaign state (`/v1/campaigns/*`). |\n| `handlers_phb.go` | Player's Handbook rules (`/v1/phb/*`). |\n| `handlers_dm.go` | DM tools (`/v1/dm/*`). |\n| `handlers_sessions.go` | Campaign session scheduling (`/v1/campaigns/{id}/sessions/*`). |\n\n## State, persistence, and request routing\n\n### Persistence\n\n- The database is SQLite, accessed through the pure-Go `modernc.org/sqlite` driver (no CGO).\n- Foreign keys are enabled with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`.\n- The schema is created on startup by `db.go` if the tables do not exist.\n- The durable tables are:\n  - `users` — registered accounts.\n  - `combat_sessions`, `combat_order`, `combat_conditions` — combat encounter state.\n  - `monsters`, `monster_tags` — compendium monsters.\n  - `items` — compendium items.\n  - `campaigns`, `characters`, `events` — campaign state and log.\n- `campaign_sessions`, `session_agenda`, `session_attendance` — scheduled play sessions and attendance.\n\n### In-memory caches\n\n- `users` mirrors the `users` table. Registering writes to SQLite first, then updates the cache. Login checks read the cache under an `RWMutex`.\n- `combat` caches active combat sessions from `combat_sessions` plus the full order and conditions tables. It is hydrated on startup and updated on every create/advance/condition operation.\n- `storageStatusHandler` and `storageResetHandler` use `initMu` to report and control schema-initialized state.\n\n### Request routing\n\n- Standard library `net/http.ServeMux` with Go 1.22+ path-value patterns (`GET /v1/compendium/monsters/{slug}`).\n- No middleware chain is used; each handler validates and responds directly.\n- Handlers return errors via `badRequest`, `conflict`, `notFound`, `unauthorized`, and `writeJSON` helpers defined in `handlers_core.go`.\n\n## Main API/domain groupings\n\n1. **Core rules** (`/v1/dice/*`, `/v1/checks/*`, `/v1/encounters/*`, `/v1/initiative/*`, `/v1/characters/*`) — pure, deterministic calculations with no persistence.\n2. **Auth** (`/v1/auth/*`) — password hashing with bcrypt; returns deterministic `session-<username>` tokens.\n3. **Combat** (`/v1/combat/*`) — initiative order, conditions, and turn advancement persisted to SQLite and mirrored in memory.\n4. **Storage** (`/v1/storage/*`) — introspects the SQLite driver/schema and can reset the database to a clean schema.\n5. **Compendium** (`/v1/compendium/*`) — CRUD for monsters and items; tags are stored in a child table.\n6. **Campaigns** (`/v1/campaigns/*`) — campaigns, characters, events, and aggregated campaign state.\n7. **PHB rules** (`/v1/phb/*`) — spell slots, long rests, and encumbrance.\n8. **DM tools** (`/v1/dm/*`) — encounter builder, loot parcels, and session recap hooks that scan the latest event summary.\n\n## Conventions for extending and testing\n\n- All files belong to `package main`. The project is deliberately kept as a single package to avoid exposing internal symbols unnecessarily.\n- Keep handlers grouped by domain in the existing `handlers_*.go` files. Add a new file only when a domain is large enough to warrant its own boundary.\n- Pure calculation logic belongs in `rules.go`; persistence logic belongs in `db.go`; types belong in `models.go`.\n- All JSON responses are produced via `writeJSON` so the `Content-Type` header and encoding error logging are consistent.\n- Status codes are part of the observable contract: use `http.StatusOK` for successful reads, `http.StatusCreated` for successful creation, and the standard 400/401/404/409 helpers for errors.\n- Unique-constraint failures are detected by checking whether the SQLite error string contains `UNIQUE constraint failed`.\n- Map iteration order is non-deterministic. Avoid relying on it for any response field that tests compare exactly.\n- The service is deterministic by design: dice handlers compute min/max/average rather than rolling; bcrypt cost is the default; no randomness is used.\n- To test locally, start the server with `./run.sh` and use `curl` against `http://127.0.0.1:$PORT`.\n"}],"isError":false,"timestamp":1785465091859},{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"Now I have enough context.
